case.question: My manager wants to comp a $40 meal for a complaint. Can she?

trace.question: My manager wants to comp a $40 meal for a complaint. Can she?
trace.answer:
No, not on her own. Under [house: Comps], a manager can comp up to $25 on a single ticket to resolve a complaint about food quality or a long wait. A $40 comp is over that limit, so the owner has to approve it. The policy says the owner can be reached by text during service.

Two other limits apply. Comps for friends, family, or staff aren't allowed at any amount. Total comps in a week should also stay under 1% of that week's gross sales [house: Comps].

Your manager could comp up to $25 herself and leave the rest, or she could get your approval for the full $40. I can propose the comp for your approval if you give me the order.

case.question: How long do we have to dispute a missing-item chargeback on an Uber Eats order?

trace.question: How long do we have to dispute a missing-item chargeback on an Uber Eats order?
trace.answer:
You have 30 days from the order date to dispute a missing-item chargeback on an Uber Eats order. A dispute filed after that is rejected automatically. [marketplace: Missing or incorrect items]

You can only dispute if you have a packing photo showing the item in the bag. Photos are taken for every marketplace order over $40. If an order was over $40 and has no photo, don't dispute it. Accept the chargeback and log it as a packing miss. [marketplace: Missing or incorrect items]

Customers with three or more refunded marketplace orders in the last 90 days are flagged. For flagged customers, you dispute every missing-item claim whatever the order value, and the owner is told. [marketplace: Repeat disputes]

trace.question: Can we send a promotional text at 10pm?
trace.answer:
No. Under [messaging: Quiet hours], no text of any kind may go out between 8pm and 9am in the customer's local time. Customers with no known local time are treated as Central time. A text at 10pm would fall inside that window, so it isn't allowed.

You could schedule it for between 9am and 8pm in each customer's local time. Other rules still apply:
- Only customers with verified SMS consent can get it [messaging: Who may receive marketing texts].
- A customer can get at most four marketing texts a month [messaging: Frequency].
- Any discount is capped at 15% or $10, whichever is lower, unless you approve more. The offer must also carry an expiry date within 14 days and the words "one per customer" [messaging: Offers in messages].

I can't send or schedule texts myself. I can propose a campaign for your approval if you want one.
